segments.text: Quiet street. Thirty zone. Speed bump ahead.
But the speed bump just snored. It has whiskers. And tusks. It's a sleeping walrus. What do you do?
Most drivers don't slow down. They just drive over it.
Big mistake. Bump! The walrus wakes up. And he is very grumpy.
He flips your car onto his nose, like a circus ball. Spins it. And falls back asleep. Still holding it. Forever.
Here's how you do it properly.
A speed bump means: slow down. So you stop. Completely.
Walruses love a back scratch. So you grab your snow brush.
Scratch, scratch. He smiles. And rolls onto his back.
Now he's the softest speed bump in town. Boing. Boing.
And he waves goodbye with his flipper.
Next exam question: a zebra is lying on the zebra crossing. Follow, so you don't miss it.
